h: שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל, מַאֲמָר י״ב Shabbos HaGadol — Maamar Yud Bais
The Firstborn Who Slew Their Fathers: Atonement for Israel's Idolatry

p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
In the Midrash
(שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים קל"ו)
(Shocher Tov, Tehillim 136)
עַל הַפָּסוּק
on the verse
(תְּהִלִּים קל"ו, י'):
(Tehillim 136:10):
לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶם
"To Him who smote Egypt through their firstborn,"
אִיתָא:
it is stated:
מִיָּד יָצְאוּ וְנָטְלוּ כָּל אֶחָד חַרְבּוֹ וְהָרַג אֶת אָבִיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
"Immediately they went out and each took his sword and slew his father, as it is said:
לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם וְכוּלֵּי
'To Him who smote Egypt, etc.'
שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא הָרְגוּ הַבְּכוֹרוֹת בַּאֲבוֹתֵיהֶם,
six hundred thousand did the firstborn slay among their fathers,"
עַיֵּין שָׁם.
(see there).
וְהַתּוֹסָפוֹת
And Tosafos
(Shabbos 87b)
כָּתְבוּ שֶׁמִּטַּעַם זֶה קוֹרִין אוֹתוֹ שַׁבָּת הַגָּדוֹל.
wrote that for this reason it is called Shabbos HaGadol.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין הַנֵּס תּוֹעֶלֶת לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
Now, ostensibly, this miracle had no utility for the Exodus from Egypt,
וְגַם כָּאן יִיחוּד "כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ" עַל "לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶם"!
and also here there is the specific refrain "for His kindness is forever" attached to "To Him who smote Egypt through their firstborn"!
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא:
The explanation is:
שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לְפַרְעֹה:
we find that Moshe Rabbeinu said to Pharaoh:
הֵן נִזְבַּח וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא יִסְקְלֻנוּ!
"If we slaughter, etc., will they not stone us?"!
וּמַה זֶּה תָּפַס לְשׁוֹן סְקִילָה וְלֹא מִיתָה סְתָם?
Why did he specifically use the term "stoning" (sekilah) rather than death in general?
אַךְ אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
However, it is stated in the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב', כ"ב):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:22):
אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, הֵיאַךְ אָנוּ נִגְאָלִין וְכָל מִצְרַיִם מְטוּנֶּפֶת מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּנוּ וְכוּלֵּי?
"They said to him: 'Moshe our teacher, how can we be redeemed when all of Egypt is defiled with our idolatry, etc.?'"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁקִּיטְרֵג עוּזָא שַׂר שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם:
And as Uza, the guardian angel of Egypt, prosecuted:
הַלָּלוּ עוֹבְדֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי!
"These are idol worshippers, etc.!"
אַךְ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר: מִשְׁכוּ וּקְחוּ,
Yet Hashem, may He be blessed, said: "Draw forth and take,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ
and they expounded
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ט"ז, ב'):
(Shemos Rabbah 16:2):
מִשְׁכוּ יְדֵיכֶם מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי.
"Withdraw your hands from idolatry, etc."
וְלָכֵן נִתְיָירֵא מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאִם נִזְבַּח תּוֹעֲבַת מִצְרַיִם, יִתְעוֹרֵר הַקִּטְרוּג אָז מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
Therefore, Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, feared that if we slaughter the abomination of Egypt, prosecution would be aroused then over their past idolatry
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁעָנוּ לְיִרְמְיָה
just as we find that the people answered Yirmiyahu
(יִרְמְיָה מ"ד, י"ז-כ"א):
(Yirmiyahu 44:17-21):
כִּי עָשֹׂה נַעֲשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר לְקַטֵּר לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְגוֹמֵר כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשִׂינוּ וְגוֹמֵר וַנִּשְׂבַּע לֶחֶם וַנִּהְיֶה טוֹבִים וְגוֹמֵר,
"For we will certainly do, etc., to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven, etc., as we did, etc., and we had plenty of food and were well off, etc.,
וּמִן אָז חָדַלְנוּ לְקַטֵּר וְגוֹמֵר חָסַרְנוּ כֹל;
and since we stopped burning incense, etc., we have lacked everything";
וְעָנָה לָהֶם יִרְמְיָה:
and Yirmiyahu answered them:
הֲלוֹא אֶת הַקִּטֵּר אֲשֶׁר קִטַּרְתֶּם וְגוֹמֵר אֹתָם זָכַר ה' וְגוֹמֵר.
"Did not the incense that you burned, etc.—them did Hashem remember, etc."
וַהֲלֹא הֵם אָמְרוּ שֶׁאָז הָיָה לָהֶם כָּל טוֹב,
Now, did they not say that back then they had every good thing?
וְלָמָּה כָּעֵת זָכַר ה' אֶת מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לְהַעֲנִישָׁם עַל הֶעָבָר,
Why, then, did Hashem remember their deeds now to punish them for the past,
וּבְעֵת שֶׁעָבְרוּ לֹא נֶעֶנְשׁוּ?!
whereas at the time they transgressed they were not punished?!
אַךְ מֵאָז שֶׁעָשׂוּ הָרַע, יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶנְשׁוּ רַק הָיָה לָהֶם טוֹב כְּדֵי לְהַאֲבִידָם;
Indeed, when they were doing evil, it could be they were not punished but given good in order to destroy them;
וְרַק אַחַר שֶׁעָזְבוּ הָרַע וְהִתְחִילוּ לָשׁוּב, אָז נִתְעוֹרֵר עֲלֵיהֶם הַקִּטְרוּג,
and only after they abandoned evil and began to repent did the prosecution awaken against them
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם יִרְמְיָה שֶׁאֹתָם זָכַר ה' וְגוֹמֵר!
and this is what Yirmiyahu told them, that "them did Hashem remember, etc."!
וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נִתְיָירֵא מִפְּנֵי הַמִּצְרִים אִם הָיָה מַסְכִּים ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּזְבְּחוּ תּוֹעֲבַת מִצְרַיִם לְעֵינֵיהֶם,
And similarly, Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, did not fear the Egyptians if Hashem, may He be blessed, agreed that they slaughter Egypt's deity before their eyes;
אַךְ נִתְיָירֵא שֶׁלֹּא יִתְעוֹרֵר אָז הַקִּטְרוּג מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
rather, he feared that prosecution over idolatry would then awaken against Israel,
שֶׁדִּינוֹ בִּסְקִילָה, וְדִין אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת לֹא בָּטְלוּ
whose penalty is stoning—and the law of the four capital punishments has never been abolished
(כְּתוּבּוֹת ל'.).
(Kesubos 30a).
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה: וְלֹא יִסְקְלֻנוּ!
And this is what Moshe meant by "will they not stone us?!"
וְה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר לָהֶם: מִשְׁכוּ יְדֵיכֶם מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּקְחוּ לָכֶם צֹאן שֶׁל מִצְוָה,
And Hashem, may He be blessed, told them: "Withdraw your hands from idolatry and take for yourselves sheep for a mitzvah,"
וּלְבַטֵּל הַקִּטְרוּג הָיָה הַנֵּס לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶם,
and to nullify the prosecution came the miracle of "To Him who smote Egypt through their firstborn,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
based on what is brought in the holy Zohar
(בְּתוֹסֶפֶת לְפָרָשַׁת בָּלָק ש"ד.):
(in the Tosefes to Parshas Balak, 304a):
מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקַרְתָּ בְעֵינַי נִכְבַּדְתָּ וְכוּלֵּי... מֵאֲשֶׁר יָקָר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי... וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ וְכוּלֵּי.
"Since you were precious (yakarta) in My eyes, you were honored, etc.... it should have said 'yakar,' etc.... 'And I will give a man in your place,' etc."
וְהוּא שֶׁהַבַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה מִיָּד עָאל וְאִתְדַּבֵּק בֵּיהּ בְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
And this is because a penitent immediately enters and cleaves to the Holy One, blessed is He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' קכ"ט.):
וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים
"And Avraham was old, advanced in days"
בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִילָּאִין,
into those supernal days,
שֶׁבֵּירֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל הַשֶּׁבַע מִדּוֹת, וְלֹא זָכָה לָזֶה רַק כַּד הֲוָה סִיב וְכוּלֵּי;
having refined himself through all seven attributes, and he did not merit this until he was old, etc.;
וְאָמַר שָׁם:
and it says there:
וּמָארֵיהוֹן דִּתְשׁוּבָה בְּשַׁעְתָּא חֲדָא בְּיוֹמָא חֲדָא בְּרִגְעָא חֲדָא קְרִיבִין לְגַבֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי.
"Whereas masters of repentance, in a single hour, in a single day, in a single moment, draw near to the Holy One, blessed is He, etc."
וְהָעֵצָה: וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ
And the stratagem is: "And I will give a man in your place"
וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דִּכְתִיב
which is like Yom Kippur, as it is written
(וַיִּקְרָא ט"ז, כ"ב):
(Vayikra 16:22):
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם,
"And the goat shall bear upon itself all their iniquities,"
וְדָרְשׁוּ
and they expounded
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ס"ה, ט"ו):
(Bereishis Rabbah 65:15):
הַשָּׂעִיר — זֶה עֵשָׂו וְכוּלֵּי, אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנֹתָם — עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם, דִּכְתִיב
"The goat—this is Esav, etc.; all their iniquities—the iniquities of the 'wholesome man' (tam), as it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ה, כ"ו):
(Bereishis 25:26):
וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם.
'And Yaakov was a wholesome man.'"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
That is, Hashem, may He be blessed, advocates in defense of Israel
שֶׁכָּל הָעֲוֹנוֹת גָּרַם עֵשָׂו, שֶׁהוּא הִכְנִיס בָּהֶם הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה,
that Esav caused all the sins by injecting the leaven in the dough into them,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנָם לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן אֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם;
whereas Israel's true desire is to do the will of their Father in Heaven;
וְזֶהוּ: וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּךָ
and this is "And I will give a man in your place"
הַהוּא אָדָם דְּאָתָא מֵעַמָּא אַחֲרָא.
that man who comes from another nation.
וְכֵן הָיָה כָּאן:
And so it happened here:
יָצְאוּ וְנָטְלוּ כָּל אֶחָד חַרְבּוֹ וְהָרַג אֶת אָבִיו,
they went out and each took his sword and slew his father
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ בְּנֵי נֹחַ, וּמִיתַת בֶּן נֹחַ לְעוֹלָם בְּסַיִף
because they were descendants of Noach, and the execution of a Noachide is always by the sword
(סַנְהֶדְרִין נ"ו.)
(Sanhedrin 56a)
וְהָרְגוּ שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא לְכַפֵּר הַקִּטְרוּג מֵעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and they slew six hundred thousand to atone for and remove the prosecution from upon Israel;
שֶׁהֵם הַמִּצְרִים הָיוּ הַחַיָּיבִים בְּמַה שֶּׁשִּׁיעְבְּדוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפָרֶךְ,
for they, the Egyptians, were the culpable ones by having enslaved Israel with crushing labor,
אַחַר כָּךְ נִטְמְעוּ בָּהֶם,
after which Israel assimilated among them;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהָיוּ תְּחִילָּתָם בְּאוֹנֶס, אַף מַה שֶּׁהָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ בְּרָצוֹן מִכָּל מָקוֹם מָצִינוּ
and since their beginning was under compulsion, even what later occurred willingly is nevertheless considered compulsion, as we find
(כְּתוּבּוֹת נ"א:)
(Kesubos 51b)
דְּחָשִׁיב אוֹנֶס: מַאי טַעְמָא? יֵצֶר אַלְבְּשַׁהּ!
that it is deemed compulsion: what is the reason? Because passion clothed her!
וְלָכֵן הָיָה הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא לְמִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
And therefore the tally was six hundred thousand, matching the number of the Children of Israel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר לְעֵיל מַאֲמָר א').
(as explained above in Maamar 1).
לָכֵן יִיחֵד הַכָּתוּב לְמַכֵּה מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ,
Therefore Scripture singled out "To Him who smote Egypt, etc., for His kindness is forever,"
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה חֶסֶד מְיוּחָד לְכַפָּרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל כָּאָמוּר.
for this was a unique kindness for the atonement of Israel, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim (Shocher Tov) 136 — When the plague of the firstborn came, the firstborn begged their fathers and Pharaoh to send the Hebrews out and were refused. "…Immediately they went out, each took his sword and killed his father, as it says, 'Who struck Egypt through their firstborn'… sixty myriads the firstborn killed among their fathers."

rich.text: Midrash Tehillim (Shocher Tov) 136

— When the plague of the firstborn came, the firstborn begged their fathers and Pharaoh to send the Hebrews out and were refused. "…Immediately they went out, each took his sword and killed his father, as it says, 'Who struck Egypt through their firstborn'… sixty myriads the firstborn killed among their fathers."

paragraphs.text: Tosafos, Shabbos 87b, s.v. V'oso yom — "…The firstborn went to their fathers and to Pharaoh to ask that he send Israel out, and they would not. The firstborn made war and killed many of them; this is 'Who struck Egypt through their firstborn.'" Therefore, Tosafos says, it is called Shabbos HaGadol.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Acharei Mos and Shabbos HaGadol 5676 — “Because Israel were destined, on the night of the Exodus, to rise to very high levels, even those sins that until then had not been counted as sins were awakened; therefore they needed additional mitzvos to stand against the prosecution of those sins. So He commanded them to take the lamb on the tenth of the month and tie it to their bedposts, and this was for Israel true self-sacrifice, as Moshe said, ‘If we slaughter the abomination of Egypt before their eyes, will they not stone us?’ And through self-sacrifice their body was considered as though it were not, so their sin could no longer be reckoned.” Connection: Shem MiShmuel shares the insight that the prosecution against Israel was awakened by their very ascent, and reads Moshe's fear of stoning in that light; he adds that the danger itself, faced in self-sacrifice, is what silenced the charge.

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 30a–b — "Rav Yosef said: from the day the Temple was destroyed, though the Sanhedrin ceased, the four deaths did not cease… one liable to stoning either falls from a roof or a beast tramples him; one liable to the sword either is handed to the government or bandits come upon him." Rashi: falling from a roof resembles stoning; the government kills with the sword.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 75 — “The sins in the soul of a Jew are not an essential acquisition but only incidental, and therefore they can be redeemed. Just as monetary holiness can be redeemed, another thing being taken in its place and the holiness falling upon it, so He transfers Israel's sins onto others, as in ‘I will give a man in your place,’ and the sins fall upon them; and as in ‘the goat shall bear upon it all their iniquities,’ as the Sages said, that He places the iniquities on the head of Esav. But the mitzvos are bodily holiness and cannot be redeemed.” Connection: The same pairing of “I will give a man in your place” with the goat that carries the sins to Esav; it grounds the transfer in the sins being incidental to a Jew while his mitzvos are his own.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach I, Ki Savo — “‘All the sicknesses of Egypt that you dreaded’: here Moshe hinted to Israel that with every plague that came upon Egypt the hearts of many souls in Israel also trembled, those who had some trace of a lack resembling theirs in some matter; they were filled with fear, and through that fear their iniquity was atoned, and Hashem gave Egypt in their place, as it is written, ‘I will give a man in your place.’ So: ‘Only with your eyes will you behold the recompense of the wicked’ — if some lack is found in you, through the fear your heart's crookedness is straightened.” Connection: The same reading that Egypt's punishment served as Israel's atonement under “I will give a man in your place”; Mei HaShiloach places the atonement in the fear Israel felt as they watched each plague.
